title: Blood for blood
summary: The Hebrew is a perfect six-word mirror (shofek dam ha-adam / ba-adam damo yishafek). The form enacts the content: the act returns on its doer.

title: The flood narrative as a single mirror

levels.label: B
levels.text: All flesh corrupt on the earth

levels.label: C
levels.text: God resolves to destroy; ark commanded

levels.label: D
levels.text: Command to enter the ark; seven days

levels.label: C'
levels.text: God resolves never to destroy; sacrifice

summary: Wenham showed that the flood story, often divided by critics into two sources, reads as one carefully balanced structure turning on 'God remembered Noah' (8:1). Even the numbers mirror: 7 days, 40 days, 150 days — 150, 40, 7.

title: Dogs and pigs

levels.label: A
levels.text: Do not give dogs what is holy
levels.quote: Do not give dogs what is holy;

levels.label: B
levels.text: do not throw your pearls before swine
levels.quote: do not throw your pearls before swine.

levels.label: B'
levels.text: they may trample them under their feet (swine)
levels.quote: If you do, they may trample them under their feet,

levels.label: A'
levels.text: and turn and tear you to pieces (dogs)
levels.quote: and then turn and tear you to pieces.

summary: Read in order, pigs both trample and tear — but pigs do not tear. The ABBA pattern assigns trampling to the pigs and tearing to the dogs.

title: The Sabbath and the human
summary: A two-line saying whose word order flips to make the point about priority.

title: Heart, ears, eyes — eyes, ears, heart

levels.label: A
levels.text: Make the hearts of this people calloused;
levels.quote: Make the hearts of this people calloused;

levels.label: C'
levels.text: Otherwise they might see with their eyes,
levels.quote: Otherwise they might see with their eyes,

levels.label: A'
levels.text: understand with their hearts, and turn and be healed.
levels.quote: understand with their hearts, and turn and be healed.”

summary: Isaiah's commission runs heart–ears–eyes, then eyes–ears–heart. Jesus quotes it in Matthew 13:14–15 to explain the parables.

title: Exalted and humbled
summary: The same reversal saying appears in Luke 14:11 and 18:14.

title: Seek me and live

levels.label: C'
levels.text: Gilgal will surely go into exile
levels.quote: for Gilgal will surely go into exile,

levels.label: B'
levels.quote: and Bethel will come to nothing.

summary: Three shrines named going in, and two named coming out — Beersheba at the centre is the one Amos does not condemn to exile, since it lay in Judah.
